title: Channels
objective: Users connect, check, start, stop and remove chat channel accounts, decide who may message the agent, look up contacts and ids, and send, broadcast, poll, react, edit, pin and thread messages through the CLI, the Control UI and the agent message tool, and talk to the agent from chat apps in direct chats, groups, threads and ambient rooms, normally with several channels running, channel turns in flight, drafts streaming and deliveries queued, and with hot reloads, platform failures, retries, restarts and crashes around them.

phases.intent: A user has the conformance channel, a Telegram account on the platform shim and a Discord account on the fixture all running at once; the probe status and channel status are observed.
A user starts a held turn on a separately routed agent and session reserved for ambient activity; its admission and background handle are recorded while ordinary conversations remain available.

An operator observes the first native pairing list consuming expired and excess fixture requests, then attempts the captured expired code and a fourth request at capacity while legacy files and pre-bootstrap approvals remain present; before and after state, native responses, owner configuration and Doctor findings are recorded.
An operator adds a second Telegram account to the running Gateway from the CLI with synthetic fixture setup; the add output, the channel list and the status are recorded.

An operator opens the Channels page and starts the existing configured Telegram account's setup wizard from Browse all and the detail's Run setup, exercising answer fields, secret reveal, docs and external links, Continue and Cancel; screens and wizard responses are recorded. Available channel: Set up is outside this recipe because the supplied Telegram fixture is already configured.

An operator runs the configure wizard channel section and the guided channels add flow under a pseudo-terminal with scripted answers. Each invocation records its native responses and resulting status, then restores its scoped configuration before the next invocation; final reads record the restored state.

An operator runs the recorded channels add and channels login commands with a different supplied CLI profile label. The helper captures the actual selected paths and native results, including custom-path precedence, and restores any scoped config changes; a path outside the owned clone prevents the mutating input.

An operator uses a supplied already installed third-party channel artifact that actually exercises the recorded legacy setup, runtime alias and identifier compatibility surfaces; native help, setup and inbound outcomes are recorded without installing another plugin.
A user adds a named second Telegram fixture account with channels add while the Gateway runs, then records the written configuration and native account status.

An operator disables config reload for one bounded observation, adds a reserved Telegram fixture account and changes group-message settings. Native config/status and foreground message observations are captured before and after an owned Gateway restart; the previous settings and account set are restored before continuing.

An operator shows and hides Advanced settings in the supplied Telegram channel form, observes the preference after page reloads, then edits the owned account display name with native Save and Reload; changed state, status and both preference and config restoration are recorded.

An operator uses explicit-account CLI login and a forced QR start/wait under one owner per flow; actual account results and cleanup are recorded. UI controls are observed in link-channel-qr-under-states.
A user starts and waits for an explicit-account QR login, then exercises native CLI default-account selection in the supplied sole-owned-account clone. Each flow owns cleanup.
A user operates real WhatsApp card and wizard QR controls in the supplied sole-owned-account clone. Native account selection, refresh/wait results and cleanup are recorded without request rewriting.

An operator lists configured and catalog channels, reads recorded and probed status, and checks overall status and health while account, workspace plugin, broken or disabled plugin, provenance and legacy configuration traits coexist; responses are recorded.

An operator opens the Channels page, refreshes it, opens a configured and an available channel's details, follows the Docs link, runs Probe, closes the detail and refreshes the Nostr and WhatsApp cards; screens and responses are recorded.

An operator runs Doctor over supplied channel, access, binding, plugin and legacy configuration, including retired Microsoft Teams conversation, poll, SSO-token and feedback JSON files; diagnostic findings and recovery guidance are recorded.
An operator on a fresh install without an agent roster and with exactly one channel lists channels, sends a message without naming the channel and checks status; outputs are recorded.
An operator in an explicit multi-agent setup without a System Agent lists channels, tries a guided add without --agent and sends a message; outputs are recorded.
A user reads the full overall status summary with --all; shared inventory, probe and Doctor observations are recorded by the corresponding status and Doctor phases.
An operator asks what each channel account can do, for all channels and for Telegram, and Kova's preflight reads the packaged message contracts; capability output is recorded.
A user asks what the Discord account can do for one channel target while a channel turn is in flight, observing the capability output.
An operator tails channel logs for all channels and for Telegram while channels run; log output is recorded.

An operator stops and restarts the conformance channel account through the Gateway and asks to start disabled, suppressed and enabled secret-unavailable Telegram accounts; the RPC responses and status are recorded.
A user stops and starts one Telegram account through Gateway methods, records native status after each operation, and reads channel status through the admin HTTP RPC.
An operator looks up self, peers, groups and group members on Telegram and the conformance channel and resolves names to ids; directory and resolve output is recorded.
A user resolves Discord channel and user names and lists its self, peers, groups and group members, observing returned identifiers. Shared Telegram directory output is recorded in look-up-directory.

A user resolves a Discord channel name using the explicit channel kind and lists conformance-channel groups, observing returned identifiers and empty or unsupported results. Shared self and peer listings are recorded by the corresponding directory phases.

An operator reviews, filters and resolves freshly captured requests through the Channels UI, including scoped first-owner bootstrap and notification; exact request actions, before and after state and restored configuration are recorded.

A user requests the native conformance allowlist listing and observes its authorization or unsupported-capability reply, then records the existing security audit, Doctor and scoped state observations.

A user exercises supplied access-group and command-authorization states through native admission and allowlist-list requests, observing admitted input, authorization or unsupported-capability replies and existing scoped state.
